For the Wind Mill primitive, we observe a statistically significant non-overlap in Wilson score intervals for completion rates across wind speed bins. This establishes a monotonic decay kernel K_wind(w) applied to the base completion probability p_0. Mathematically, p(w) = p_0 * exp(-lambda * w), where lambda is empirically derived from the 0-14 vs >=20 mph bins. The Cold Mill operator introduces a step-function perturbation to the Expected Points Added (EPA) distribution. By comparing the EPA per dropback in temperatures <= 25F against the baseline 26-70F regime, we isolate a negative drift term delta_EPA_cold. This reflects the physical degradation of ball handling and throwing mechanics. Finally, the Roof Mill primitive operates on the second moment of the scoring distribution. The shift from outdoor to enclosed stadiums reduces the stochastic noise floor, compressing the standard deviation of game totals while elevating the mean. These three operators form a cohesive environmental adjustment layer, allowing the GSE to dynamically recalibrate its predictive priors based on real-time stadium telemetry. Failure modes arise when sample sizes in extreme bins become too sparse, necessitating Bayesian shrinkage toward the global mean.
